abstract_sentences.text: Machine unlearning seeks to efficiently remove the influence of selected data while preserving generalization.

evidence.anchor: Machine unlearning seeks to efficiently remove the influence of selected data while preserving generalization.

abstract_sentences.text: Significant progress has been made in low dimensions, where p is much smaller than n, but proportional high dimensions p ∼ n pose serious theoretical challenges because standard optimization assumptions rarely hold simultaneously.
qualifiers: low dimensions vs proportional high dimensions
abstract_sentences.comparison: low-dimensional prior work vs proportional regime

evidence.anchor: high dimensions, including proportional regimes p ∼ n, pose serious theoretical challenges

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we introduce ε-Gaussian certifiability, a canonical and robust notion well-suited to high-dimensional regimes, that optimally captures a broad class of noise adding mechanisms.
abstract_sentences.relation: answers the gap with a privacy notion

evidence.anchor: we introduce ε-Gaussian certifiability, a canonical and robust notion

abstract_sentences.text: Then we theoretically analyze the performance of a widely used unlearning algorithm based on one step of the Newton method in the high-dimensional setting described above.

evidence.anchor: theoretically analyze the performance of a widely used unlearning algorithm based on one step

abstract_sentences.text: Our analysis shows that a single Newton step, followed by a well-calibrated Gaussian noise, is sufficient to achieve both privacy and accuracy in this setting.

evidence.anchor: a single Newton step, followed by a well-calibrated Gaussian noise, is sufficient

abstract_sentences.text: This result stands in sharp contrast to the only prior work that analyzes machine unlearning in high dimensions, Zou et al. (2025), which relaxes some standard optimization assumptions but operates under ε-certifiability.

evidence.anchor: sharp contrast to the only prior work that analyzes machine unlearning in high dimensions

abstract_sentences.text: That work concludes that at least two steps are required to ensure both privacy and accuracy.

evidence.anchor: at least two steps are required to ensure both privacy and accuracy

abstract_sentences.text: Our result leads us to conclude that the discrepancy in the number of steps arises because ε-certifiability is suboptimal and incompatible with noise adding mechanisms, which ε-Gaussian certifiability overcomes optimally.
abstract_sentences.relation: attributes the discrepancy to the criterion

final_judgment.single_storyline: Conditional hypothesis testing supplies a Gaussian trade-off privacy target; one Newton deletion step controls its residual, and calibrated isotropic Gaussian noise then yields GPAR plus a vanishing GED in the stated proportional GLM regime. The empirical sequence tests p, ε, m, baseline notion and data regime in that order.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body retains RERM/deletion interfaces, Definitions 1–3, Gaussian trade-off and GED equations, one-step mechanism, A/B assumptions, Theorems 2–3, m scaling, Figures 1–5 and the main conclusion.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix B–I move motivations, prior-work scaling failures, constants and calibration, proofs, the sub-Gaussian extension argument, UED, and n=p/2/additional plots. The core decision remains readable in the body, while sharp constants and proof audit require the appendix.
final_judgment.best_pattern: The most effective pattern is equation (5)–(10) reducing arbitrary tests to a one-dimensional Gaussian trade-off, followed by equations (59)–(62) that make the residual-to-GPAR chain explicit; Figures 1–3 align log-scale sweeps with p, ε and m predictions.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The causal explanation for the two-step versus one-step discrepancy is not independently identified: Figure 4 changes certifiability/noise baseline together, and the central residual bound is imported from Zou et al. The sub-Gaussian extension in H is a proof sketch rather than a new line-by-line derivation.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For noisy unlearning, define the adversary test and trade-off target before optimizing the update; make the noise scale, residual bound, prediction metric and evidence plots form one auditable chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits continuous high-dimensional parameter releases with approximate unlearning. Discrete outputs, non-convex deep models, p≫n, distribution-level deletion and online requests need a new baseline trade-off, residual theorem and identification design.
